newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - June 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The latest survey by independent consulting group Rainmaker Information Services Pty Ltd reveals the popular industry superannuation funds are not competitive with their main Government and corporate super fund rivals. The survey shows industry funds earned an average of 6.8 per cent a year for the past three years, in contrast with Government and corporate funds which earned 8 and 11 per cent respectively over the same period. Page 1.

The Federal Government has limited payments of the A$800 million diesel fuel rebate to mining companies, in a decision which is contrary to an understanding the industry believed it had reached with the Government in return for the acceptance of tougher tax break eligibility rules. Industry leaders will demand the decision be reversed at a meeting later this month. Page 1.

Federal Finance Minister John Fahey says Commonwealth-State financial relations should be examined as part of the tax reform debate. Opposition treasury spokesman Gareth Evans says Labor will also develop a tax reform package for the next election. Page .

A report from the Australian Taxation Office's cash economy task force has called for a range of strategies to attack the cash economy more effectively. The measures include a more visible audit program in identified sectors and educational programs to target industries where unrecorded cash transactions are common. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A joint task force report on the multi-million dollar black economy, to be released by the Australian Taxation Office this week, recommends that incentives be offered to individuals to turn in tax cheats, and that recalcitrant businesses be offered a tax amnesty. Other measures suggested to control the cash economy include encouraging consumers to report cash transactions to the tax office. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard and Opposition Leader Kim Beazley are to meet this week to discuss ways of preventing a double dissolution election on the Federal Government's race powers. Both sides of politics agree the prospect would be detrimental to the welfare of the nation. Page 1.

The family of nurse Yvonne Gilford, who was killed in Saudi Arabia, claim relatives of the two British nurses accused of her murder will be wasting their time if they fly to Australia to plead for mercy. Yvonne's father Frank Gilford believes the death penalty is the appropriate punishment, and Laurel Gilford says they will not talk to any relatives. Page 3.

The Australian Medical Association has warned doctors will limit bulk-bulling and charge higher fees unless the Federal Government reviews the health system. AMA vice-president David Brand said the AMA had few choices but to encourage GPs to consider stopping after-hours visits and charging higher services in order to protect their incomes. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Documents filed with Administrative Services Minister David Jull, and obtained under Freedom of Information legislation, reveal overseas investigations of Tasmanian onions consumed in Madrid, a feud between the Greeks and Turks, and the cleaning up of rivers in Pittsburgh were three issues cited as justification for overseas trips by MPs. Page 1.

Breaking a 23-year silence, one of New South Wales' most notorious criminals, John Lewthwaite, who is serving time for the brutal 1974 murder of five year old Nicole Hanns, says he believes politics are keeping him in prison. Lewthwaite has been eligible for parole for three years but was recently rejected for day release. Page 1.

Hong Kong and Los Angeles-based property developer David Brice, a former Channel 9 newsreader, has proposed an A$800 million plan to amalgamate the Royal Automobile Club on Macquarie Street with the adjacent Quay apartments, which would lead to the tearing down of the apartment complex at East Circular Quay. Page 1.

Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said the Federal Government had no choice but to go ahead with further cuts to car industry protection due to the high tariffs on the poor and on export industries. Treasurer Peter Costello received the final report of the Productivity Commission's inquiry into car tariffs last week. Page 3.
THE AGE

Prime Minister John Howard has released a Commonwealth submission to the High Court in February 1996, which shows the then Labor Government had opposed paying compensation to six Aborigines taken from their families in the Northern Territory between 1918 and 1953. Howard says the document shows the Labor Party has made a "huge backflip" on the stolen children issue. Page A1.

Victorian mountaineer Brigette Muir, 39, yesterday arrived in Kathmandu after last week becoming the first Australian woman to climb Mount Everest. Muir said all she wanted was a bath, a bed, and a few gin and tonics. Muir said she felt her feat was "just fantastic". Page A1.

A study by Monash University has found ghetto suburbs are forming in Australian cities, as they become more deeply divided along class lines and manufacturing jobs disappear. The study found the rich and poor are increasingly living in separate suburbs. age A1.

Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett says a range of measures may be taken to ensure retailers pass on the A$104 million fuel tax cut, including new legislation which would make retailers display the wholesale and retail price of petrol. The tax cut of A4.1 cents for a litre of diesel, and A1.6 cents per litre for petrol took effect yesterday. Page A3.
